svg.text: S5-A RING RACK — a paternoster without turns
Two touching columns of cradles per lane form a closed ring: push across at top and bottom, lift one column, lower the other.
worst 20 s, mean 10 s (1.3 s per step)
ZOOM: the exit at the top of lane B
column M sinks one level per step
cradle = S box (108) + M box (162) = 270 mm
ONE INDEX STEP = ONE TURN OF THE CAMSHAFT
all three rings move together; reversed camshaft = ring runs backwards
Cams also drive the pawls that hold each column between steps;
4 gas springs carry the column weight.
WHY IT IS DENSE: what fills
S5-A ring rack: 168 places, 56 % box volume

g.text: 1/6 The order: the green M box sits in cradle F9. Each lane is a closed ring of 28 cradles in two touching columns: front F, rear M.
2/6 Index step, repeated 5 times: (a) fork pushes F14 back onto M14, bar pushes M0 forward to F0; (b) column F rises 1 level; (c) column M sinks 1 level.
3/6 The green box has reached the exit F14. The top fork shifts that cradle 137 mm to the rear, so the M box is under the roof hatch.
4/6 The gallery opens the spring flap, hooks the box under its rims and lifts it out. Boxes never slide: only the cradles move.
5/6 Put-away: the gallery lowers a returned box into the free place, the flap closes, the fork shifts the cradle back.
6/6 Camshaft backwards = ring runs the other way, so the store always takes the shorter way: worst 15 steps = 20 s, mean 10 s.
